runs.sql: SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(t2.text, '\(([0-9]+) wt% solids\)', 1) AS INTEGER) - CAST(regexp_extract(t1.text, '\(([0-9]+) wt% solids\)', 1) AS INTEGER) AS delta FROM lines t1, lines t2 WHERE t1.id = 'p8.L63' AND t2.id = 'p8.L64'

rendered: In the viscosity comparison Fig. 8[1], the NMP-processed slurries of NMC 532[2] (PVDF binder) are at 45 wt% solids[3], while the water-processed slurries (PVDF latex with CMC binder) are at 65 wt% solids[4]. Replacing the PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC therefore raises the solids content by 20[5] percentage points.

source.label: Fig. 8
source.caption: Fig. 8. Viscosity of NMC 532 cathode slurries processed in NMP (45 wt% solids) and water (65 wt% solids). The cathode compositions are NMC 532/Denka carbon black/Solvay 5130 PVDF (90/5/5/wt%) for NMP processing and NMC 532/Denka carbon black/PVDF Latex (Solvay Solef® CPH-859)/ Carboxymethylcellulose (CMC, Mw¼250,000 g/mol; DS¼0.9) (90/5/4/1 wt %) for water-based processing.
